name: Codex CLI
title: Codex CLI integration: replay sessions on cheaper models
description: Run rightmodeler on the Codex rollouts already on disk: it reads each session as a trace and judges cheaper models against the result you accepted.
lede: Codex CLI already writes every session to disk as a rollout log. rightmodeler reads those files where they sit, measures cheaper candidates against accepted outputs, and reports the result turn by turn.
tldr: rightmodeler ingests Codex CLI rollout logs straight from ~/.codex/sessions with a dedicated adapter, no export step, because the JSONL files are already on your machine. The adapter keys on the session_meta record, takes the model from each turn_context, gathers that turn's user messages and assistant output from the response_item records, and derives per-turn usage from the token_count events. Each turn is then replayed against cheaper candidates and scored against the answer Codex gave.

steps.label: 01 · Locate
steps.title: Your sessions are already on disk
steps.body: Codex CLI writes each session to ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl as you work. There is nothing to export and nothing to instrument; choose one rollout or a day's folder.

steps.label: 02 · Ingest
steps.title: Autodetected, then folded turn by turn
steps.body: The adapter recognizes a rollout from its session_meta record (id, cwd, cli_version, model_provider) alongside turn_context, response_item, and event_msg lines. The session id becomes the trace, each turn_context opens a turn with its own model and turn_id, user messages become that turn's inputs, and assistant messages, function calls, tool-call outputs, and search calls become its output. Reasoning items and world-state metadata are skipped.

steps.label: 03 · Replay + judge
steps.title: Cheaper candidates, judged against what you accepted
steps.body: Each turn is replayed against cheaper candidates through the route you choose: the OpenAI-compatible endpoint you name with --base-url and --api-key-env, or, with --route codex-login, the codex CLI you are signed in to, on your ChatGPT plan. A configured external evaluator scores the outputs when it is reachable; otherwise the built-in judge runs two calls with the reference and candidate positions swapped, at temperature zero on an API route, choosing a judge from a vendor that is neither the candidate's nor the reference's. Verdicts are confidence lower bounds kept separate per evaluator kind.

steps.label: 04 · Report + apply
steps.title: A report, and the call stays yours
steps.body: The run writes report.md with a verdict per step family, rightmodeler report --output json prints the full JSON report from the local store, and --output jsonl streams events as the run works. Thin evidence produces an abstention with a named reason. When a family clears every release gate, rightmodeler apply opens a draft pull request that changes model identifiers and nothing else, watch reconciles it against CI, and rollback restores the pre-apply files, refusing unless every restored digest matches.

setup.intro: Nothing to install: npx runs the published CLI, and init finds your Codex rollouts on disk automatically. An interactive init asks how to call models and remembers the answer for the repository: an API key for a provider or gateway, or the plans you are signed in to on this machine, through your own codex and claude CLIs. rightmodeler never reads your logins, and it keeps API key variables away from those CLIs.

useCases.title: Audit a stretch of coding sessions
useCases.body: Rollouts accumulate under one dated tree, so the audit can take a day or a week in a pass and show which step families genuinely earned the model they ran on, across everything you did.

useCases.title: Evidence before you change the default model
useCases.body: Instead of flipping your Codex model config and watching for regressions, replay the sessions you already ran and read the per-family verdicts first. The decision gets made on evidence from your own work, not a leaderboard.

useCases.title: Per-turn usage, not a running total
useCases.body: Codex reports cumulative token counts. The adapter subtracts each turn's baseline from the running total, so a turn's usage is its own rather than the session's so far, which keeps the cost side of the comparison honest.

useCases.title: Replay through your plan
useCases.body: No API key needed: --route codex-login replays candidates through the codex CLI you are signed in to, and --judge-route claude-login has the claude CLI you are signed in to judge them, because the judge must come from a vendor other than both the candidates' and the recorded model's (an API key for a multi-vendor gateway can judge instead). The calls count against your plans' usage limits, the same limits as your own sessions: when one is reached the run stops and names the reset time, and rerunning the same command after the reset picks up where the run stopped. These calls write no session files, so they never turn up in the rollouts you audit next.

limits: It reads rollout files from disk. It does not hook into Codex, watch live sessions, or change your Codex configuration; acting on the report stays your move.
Replay needs plain-text model call sites in the repository it scans; session files are read as traces, and the audit is built for the model calls your own code makes.

A turn needs a turn_context with a model, and a response item needs a turn to attach to. Items that arrive before any turn context, or with an unrecognized payload type, are dropped with a recorded reason rather than guessed at.
Turns that produced no assistant output are left out entirely, so a session of interrupted turns can yield fewer steps than it appears to contain.

Codex does not log dollar cost. Historical spend is not derived from the rollout; candidate calls are priced from what your replay endpoint reports and marked as an estimate when the provider returns none. Calls through a plan are priced at list price from a public model list, always as an estimate: a list-price equivalent, not a bill.

Through a plan, rightmodeler measures the model inside a coding CLI, not the API your app calls: codex adds its own instructions and your global ~/.codex/AGENTS.md to every call, cannot set temperature or an output cap, does not report which model answered, and keeps a code tool and a patch tool registered that no setting removes, so a call can include a tool step its output does not show. The report labels this. Only cases made of system or developer messages and one user message replay that way; multi-turn cases are left out with a named reason.

Plan routes run only on your own machine: rightmodeler refuses one when CI is set, and Mode B confirmation and --detach stay on an API route. Plan routes have no default limit on calls or spend: a run makes as many calls as it needs, and your plan's usage limit is the only stop.

Evidence minimums are per evaluator kind: at least 10 assessed executions, at least two distinct step IDs, and at least five distinct trajectories. Below any of those the family abstains with a named reason instead of recommending.
It is a report, not a gateway. Nothing sits between Codex and its provider, and there is no rightmodeler server to see your sessions.

faq.q: Where does Codex CLI keep its session logs?
faq.a: In ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl, one JSONL file per session, written as you work. Pass a rollout or a day's folder with --traces; the format is autodetected from the session_meta record and the turn_context and response_item lines that follow it.

faq.q: Do I need to export anything before running the audit?
faq.a: No. Codex already writes its rollouts to local disk, so there is no dashboard to visit and no export API to call. Replay needs either the key for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint you replay through, or no key at all with --route codex-login --judge-route claude-login, which run through the codex and claude CLIs you are signed in to. npx rightmodeler docs model-routes prints the full guide to both routes.

faq.q: Does rightmodeler change which model Codex uses?
faq.a: Not on its own. It produces per-family verdicts with the evidence attached, and where a family clears every gate it opens a draft pull request against your repository that you review and merge. Nothing hooks into Codex or intercepts its traffic.

faq.q: How does it count tokens for a turn?
faq.a: From the token_count events. Codex reports a running total, so the adapter takes the total at the end of a turn and subtracts the total carried in from the previous one, falling back to the last-call usage when no total is present.

faq.q: Does my session data leave my machine?
faq.a: Only during replay, when step inputs go to candidate models and the judge: through the endpoint you configured, under your own key, the same class of call Codex made to produce the log in the first place, or through the codex and claude CLIs you are signed in to, where OpenAI and Anthropic handle them under your plan accounts' data settings. There is no rightmodeler server and no account.

faq.q: What about turns where Codex ran commands or edited files?
faq.a: Those tool calls and their outputs are part of the turn's recorded output, so the judge sees what the model actually did rather than a stripped answer. Where a turn's result can feed later model-authored steps, confirmation runs your pipeline in a container with the candidate swapped in, and without a --modeb-config the recommendation stays unconfirmed.
